Data Sourcing and Generation Steps:

1. SYNC
   Source: the ORE Engine fork's own Examples/ directory (see
   external/ore/packages/methodology.txt step 1 for cloning/updating the
   checkout -- the same checkout backs both the engine binary package
   and these examples, and both should always be synced from the same
   commit).
   Script: external/ore/tools/update_ore_samples.sh
   Command:
     ./external/ore/tools/update_ore_samples.sh <path-to-ore-engine-checkout>
   Target: external/ore/examples/ (verbatim rsync --delete of Examples/,
   minus ORE's own pytest test-harness files -- conftest.py,
   ore_examples_helper.py, ore_wrapper.py, run_examples_testsuite.py,
   copy_out_expected.sh, Readme.md -- this repo vendors the example DATA,
   not the harness for running all of them via pytest) +
   external/ore/examples/manifest.json (sync provenance, written
   alongside, not inside the tree). The same invocation also syncs
   external/ore/xsd/ (see that directory's own methodology.txt) and then
   runs scripts/validate_ore_examples.sh automatically -- xsd/ and
   examples/ must always move together, since a schema/example version
   mismatch produces spurious validation failures that have nothing to
   do with either side being genuinely wrong (see step 2).

2. VALIDATE
   Command (run automatically by step 1 unless --skip-validate):
     ./scripts/validate_ore_examples.sh
   Every *.xml under external/ore/examples/ is validated against
   external/ore/xsd/input.xsd. A failure here after a sync means either
   a genuine regression in the example XML, or (more likely, if this
   repo's xsd/ was allowed to drift out of lockstep with examples/) a
   schema mismatch -- re-run step 1 without --skip-validate rather than
   silencing a real failure.

3. SPOT-CHECK AGAINST THE PACKAGED ENGINE (recommended, not automatic)
   Since examples/ExpectedOutput/ reference values were generated by
   whatever ORE build originally produced them (upstream's own CI, not
   necessarily the exact commit vendored here), a byte-exact diff
   against a freshly built engine's own output is expected to show
   small floating-point noise (see external/ore/tools/compare_csv.py's
   own doc) and, across enough of a version gap, legitimate new/removed
   report columns. external/ore/tools/package_ore.sh's own self-test
   already does this for one example (TA002_IR_Swap) automatically on
   every package build; to check others, run the packaged engine
   directly against any example's Input/ and diff with compare_csv.py:
     ore-<version>-x64-linux <path-to-example>/Input/ore.xml
     external/ore/tools/compare_csv.py <produced>/Output/npv.csv \
         <path-to-example>/ExpectedOutput/npv.csv

4. VERIFY
   Every vendored file is independently re-derivable: re-run step 1
   against the same engine_commit and diff the regenerated
   manifest.json's own tree_sha256 against what's committed -- byte-for-
   byte reproducible, no manual curation anywhere in this directory.

5. COMMIT
   Commit the synced tree + both manifest.json files (examples/ and
   xsd/) together -- they're generated from the same engine_commit and
   should never be committed out of step with each other. Never
   hand-edit a vendored example or schema file directly; if an example
   needs a fix, fix it upstream (git@github.com:OreStudio/Engine.git)
   and re-sync.
